He was captured during the Tokugawa persecution and subjected to the water torture of tsurushi. He refused to renounce his faith and died a martyr, becoming the first Filipino saint.
prayer: I am a Christian, and I will die for God.

name: Louis de Montfort
tagline: Promoter of the Rosary and 'True Devotion to Mary'.
description: Louis was a tireless missionary who traveled across western France, preaching the Gospel and the Rosary. He founded the Company of Mary and the Daughters of Wisdom and wrote the classic 'True Devotion to the Blessed Virgin'.
prayer: To Jesus through Mary.

name: Louis IX
tagline: St. Louis IX was a devout king known for his strong sense of justice and leading two crusades.
description: St. Louis IX ruled as King of France from 1226 until his death in 1270, exemplifying the role of a monarch devoted to his faith and his people. He famously led the Seventh and Eighth Crusades and worked tirelessly to promote peace and social justice throughout his realm. His dedication to charity and the care of the poor earned him lasting reverence in the Catholic Church, ultimately leading to his canonization in 1297.
prayer: If I could be king of France on such conditions as these, I would be satisfied.

name: Louis Martin
tagline: Father of St. Thérèse of Lisieux, a watchmaker and devoted father who raised five daughters who all became nuns.
description: St. Louis Martin was a French watchmaker and the father of St. Thérèse of Lisieux. Together with his wife Zélie, he raised five daughters who all entered religious life. After his wife's death, he supported his daughters' vocations with profound faith. He suffered from cerebral arteriosclerosis in his later years, enduring his affliction with great patience.
prayer: God has given me many crosses, but He has also given me much grace.

name: Louise de Marillac
tagline: Co-founder of the Daughters of Charity alongside St. Vincent de Paul.
description: St. Louise de Marillac was a pioneering figure in the 17th century, dedicated to serving the poor and marginalized in society. She established the Daughters of Charity to further St. Vincent de Paul's mission of charitable service and education. Her legacy continues to inspire countless individuals in acts of compassion and social justice worldwide.
prayer: We must strive to be all things to all people.

name: Lucy
tagline: A brave virgin martyr whose name means 'light', symbolizing her faith amid persecution.
description: St. Lucy was a Christian martyr who lived during the Diocletian persecution in the early 4th century. She is remembered for her unwavering faith and dedication to God, which ultimately led to her tragic death. Her story serves as an inspiration to many, especially those enduring struggles related to vision and clarity.
prayer: I choose to be a Christian, and I will endure any suffering for my faith.

name: Luke of Simferopol
tagline: A brilliant surgeon, professor, and archbishop who continued to serve the sick even while in Soviet exile.
description: Dr. Valentin Voyno-Yasenetsky was a world-class surgeon who wrote 'Essays on Purulent Surgery', a textbook used for decades. He became a priest and then a bishop during the height of Stalin's purges. He spent 11 years in various prisons and exiles, often performing surgeries with limited tools to save the lives of fellow prisoners.
prayer: I have loved medicine, but I loved my God more.

name: Luke the Evangelist
tagline: Author of the Gospel of Luke and the Acts of the Apostles, highlighting Jesus' compassion and the spread of Christianity.
description: St. Luke the Evangelist was a physician and a companion of St. Paul, known for his deep intellect and artistic flair. He penned the Gospel that emphasizes the mercy of Christ and the role of the Holy Spirit in the early Church. His writings have profoundly influenced Christian theology and practice throughout the centuries.
prayer: For behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.

name: Lydia
tagline: The first recorded convert to Christianity in Europe.
description: St. Lydia was a wealthy seller of purple cloth from Thyatira who became the first European convert to Christianity after hearing St. Paul preach. She opened her home to Paul and his companions and was instrumental in establishing the early Church in Philippi. Her generous spirit and faithfulness made her a key figure in the spread of the Gospel in the Roman Empire.
prayer: Faith is the light that illuminates the dark places of our lives.

name: Lydwine of Schiedam
tagline: Known for her extraordinary suffering and mystical experiences, which inspired many to a deeper faith.
description: St. Lydwine was a Dutch mystic who experienced a series of debilitating illnesses from a young age. Despite her intense suffering, she found solace in her faith and had numerous visions, serving as a spiritual guide for her community. Her profound journey and dedication led to her being revered as a saint and the patroness of the sick.
prayer: In sickness and suffering, I found the depths of God's love.

name: Magdalen of Canossa
tagline: Founding the Canossian Daughters of Charity.
description: St. Magdalen of Canossa was an Italian nun and the founder of a religious order dedicated to the spiritual and educational needs of the poor and marginalized. She devoted her life to serving others, establishing several schools and residences throughout Italy. Her legacy continues through the Canossian Sisters, who continue her mission of charity and education around the world.
prayer: To love is to give oneself without reserve.

name: Magdalena of Nagasaki
tagline: A Japanese Augustinian tertiary who was martyred during the brutal persecution of Christians in 17th-century Japan.
description: St. Magdalena of Nagasaki was the daughter of Japanese Christian martyrs. She became an Augustinian tertiary and served as an interpreter and catechist for missionaries. During the severe Tokugawa persecution, she was arrested and subjected to the torture of tsurushi (being hung upside down over a pit) for 13 days before dying.
prayer: I am a Christian and I will die a Christian.

name: Malachy
tagline: St. Malachy was a significant reformer of the Irish Church and the first native-born Archbishop of Armagh.
description: St. Malachy was born in 1094 in Armagh, Ireland, and dedicated his life to revitalizing the ecclesiastical structure of his country. His tireless efforts in reform led to a more devout and unified church, earning him recognition as one of Ireland's greatest saints. He died in 1148, leaving a lasting legacy of peace and leadership in the Irish Church.
prayer: Let us pray for the peace of the Church.

name: Mamertus
tagline: Being the Bishop of Vienne and advocating for festivals of penance and prayer.
description: St. Mamertus was the Bishop of Vienne who is best known for instituting the Rogation Days, which were intended to ask for God's mercy in times of calamity. His dedication to prayer and penance reflects the early Church's understanding of communal needs during crises. He played a crucial role in the religious life of his community during the tumultuous times of the 5th century.
prayer: Prayer is an all-powerful weapon.

name: Marcellin Champagnat
tagline: Founder of the Marist Brothers, dedicated to the education of youth.
description: St. Marcellin Champagnat was a French priest who recognized the urgent need for educational reform for the young. He established the Marist Brothers in 1817, emphasizing a curriculum rich in faith and moral values. His legacy continues through the thousands of Marist schools worldwide that serve youth in diverse communities.
prayer: To teach is to touch a life forever.

name: Marcellinus
tagline: St. Marcellinus is known for being a Pope and for his martyrdom during the persecution of Christians under Emperor Diocletian.
description: St. Marcellinus served as Pope at a time of great turmoil for Christians in the Roman Empire. He was eventually arrested and executed for his faith, becoming a symbol of courage and steadfastness. His legacy continues to inspire those who face persecution for their beliefs.
prayer: The blood of martyrs is the seed of the Church.

name: Marcellus I
tagline: He was the Pope who served during a time of intense persecution of Christians in the early Church.
description: St. Marcellus I was elected Pope in 308 AD and worked tirelessly to maintain the unity of the Church amid growing threats. He faced significant challenges from both outside and within the Christian community due to the ongoing persecutions under Emperor Maxentius. His commitment to the faith and the welfare of the Christian community has left a lasting legacy in the Church.
prayer: To speak to God is not to speak

name: Margaret Clitherow
tagline: Margaret Clitherow was a laywoman and martyr recognized for her unwavering commitment to the Catholic faith during the English Reformation.
description: St. Margaret Clitherow was born in England and became a devoted wife and mother who bravely hid priests to protect them from persecution. Her actions led to her arrest and trial, where she refused to betray her faith, ultimately sacrificing her life for her beliefs. Recognized as a martyr for her courage, she inspires many to stand firm in their convictions.
prayer: I die a Catholic, for the faith I have received.

name: Margaret Mary Alacoque
tagline: St. Margaret Mary Alacoque is renowned for her role in promoting the devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
description: Born in France, St. Margaret Mary Alacoque was a nun of the Visitation Order who received mystical revelations about the love of Jesus towards humanity. Her profound experiences led her to advocate for the devotion to the Sacred Heart, emphasizing the importance of Christ's love and mercy. She founded the First Friday devotion and contributed to the establishment of the Feast of the Sacred Heart in the Church calendar.
prayer: Behold this Heart which has loved men so much.

name: Margaret of Antioch
tagline: A virgin martyr who reportedly defeated a dragon through the sign of the cross.
description: Margaret was disowned by her father for her conversion. She was tortured and imprisoned, and according to legend, she was swallowed by a dragon in her cell but emerged unharmed when the cross she held caused the dragon to burst open.
prayer: My faith in Christ is my strength.

name: Margaret of Cortona
tagline: Known for her life of penitence and dedication to the poor after a life of sin.
description: St. Margaret of Cortona was a 13th-century Italian saint who transformed her life from one of sin and comfort to one of deep devotion and charity after a personal tragedy. Having lost her lover, she embraced a life of penance, dedicating herself to helping the poor and living in a manner wholly devoted to God. Her legacy continues to inspire those who seek redemption and a deeper relationship with Christ.
prayer: In the depth of my sin, God's mercy found me.

name: Margaret of Hungary
tagline: A Hungarian princess who willingly embraced a life of extreme penance and prayer as a Dominican nun.
description: St. Margaret was a daughter of King Béla IV of Hungary who was offered to God as a child in thanksgiving for the country's deliverance from the Mongol invasion. She entered a Dominican convent on an island in the Danube (now Margaret Island, Budapest) and chose to live a life of extreme penance, refusing all offers of marriage from European royalty.
prayer: I would rather die than leave my convent.

name: Margaret of Scotland
tagline: Reforming the Scottish church and her dedication to helping the poor.
description: St. Margaret of Scotland was an English princess who became queen consort of Scotland in the 11th century. She was instrumental in reforming the Scottish church and was known for her unwavering charity towards the poor and her dedication to education and welfare. Her legacy continues to inspire many, emphasizing the power of compassion and service to others.
prayer: What you do for the least of these, you do for me.

name: Marguerite Bays
tagline: A Swiss laywoman and mystic who received the stigmata and lived a life of extraordinary prayer and charity as a simple seamstress.
description: St. Marguerite Bays was a Swiss seamstress who lived a hidden life of extraordinary holiness. She was miraculously healed of intestinal cancer and received the stigmata, experiencing the wounds of Christ every Friday. Despite these mystical gifts, she continued her humble life of sewing, teaching catechism, and caring for the sick.
prayer: God does not ask great things of us, only small things with great love.

name: Marguerite Bourgeoys
tagline: Foundress of the Congregation of Notre Dame, known for her dedication to educating girls in New France.
description: St. Marguerite Bourgeoys was a pioneering French educator who established schools in the New World, dedicated to the spiritual and academic formation of young girls. She founded the Congregation of Notre Dame, which played a crucial role in the development of education in Canada. Her legacy continues to inspire teaching and community service to this day.
prayer: In the little things, we find great love.

name: Marguerite d'Youville
tagline: Founder of the Grey Nuns dedicated to serving the impoverished in Canada.
description: St. Marguerite d'Youville was a devoted Canadian widow known for her unyielding commitment to the less fortunate. In the face of personal hardship, she established the Grey Nuns, who became instrumental in providing care for the poor and the sick in the 18th century. Her legacy of compassion and service continues to inspire countless individuals around the world.
prayer: Let us embrace our trials with love and continue to trust in God.

name: María de Jesús Sacramentado
tagline: A Mexican foundress who established the Daughters of the Sacred Heart to serve the poor and abandoned.
description: St. María de Jesús Sacramentado Venegas de la Torre was a Mexican religious sister who founded the Daughters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. She dedicated over 50 years to caring for the sick, poor, and abandoned in Guadalajara. She persevered through the Mexican Revolution and Cristero War.
prayer: The Sacred Heart of Jesus is the fountain of all graces.

name: Maria Goretti
tagline: A courageous young martyr who exemplified forgiveness and purity.
description: St. Maria Goretti was a twelve-year-old Italian girl who became a martyr for her faith and commitment to purity. She forgave her attacker with her dying words, embodying the virtue of forgiveness and leaving a profound impact on the Catholic Church. Canonized in 1950, her life continues to inspire many to uphold the values of faith and resilience.
prayer: I forgive Alessandro and I want him to be with me in Heaven.

name: María Guadalupe García Zavala
tagline: A Mexican co-foundress who sheltered persecuted priests and the Archbishop of Guadalajara during the Cristero War.
description: St. María Guadalupe García Zavala co-founded the Handmaids of St. Margaret Mary to serve the sick and poor. During the Cristero War, she risked her life by hiding persecuted priests and even the Archbishop of Guadalajara in her hospital. She was canonized by Pope Francis in 2013.
prayer: Charity and suffering go hand in hand.

name: Maria Mazzarello
tagline: Co-founder of the Salesian Sisters (Daughters of Mary Help of Christians).
description: Maria was a hardworking peasant girl who, after surviving typhus, founded a workshop to teach needlework to young girls and provide them with a Christian education. She teamed up with Don Bosco to form a women's branch of his Salesian mission.
prayer: Be cheerful at all times.

name: Maria of Gatchina
tagline: A bedridden nun and martyr who was a source of spiritual strength for thousands during the Soviet era.
description: Maria suffered from Parkinson's disease which left her completely paralyzed and in constant pain. Despite this, she was transformed into a spiritual elder who could read souls. People lined up outside her house in Gatchina to receive her counsel. She was finally arrested and died in a prison hospital.
prayer: God is our strength

name: Mariam Baouardy
tagline: A Palestinian Carmelite mystic known as 'The Little Arab' who received the stigmata and visions.
description: Also known as St. Mary of Jesus Crucified, she was a barely literate peasant girl from I'billin. She founded the Carmelite convent in Bethlehem and was known for her extraordinary spiritual gifts, including levitation and deep mystical insight.
prayer: Holy Spirit, inspire me

name: Mariam Thresia Chiramel
tagline: An Indian mystic and foundress who established the Congregation of the Holy Family to serve the sick and marginalized in Kerala.
description: St. Mariam Thresia Chiramel Mankidiyan was an Indian mystic of the Syro-Malabar Church who experienced extraordinary spiritual phenomena from childhood. She founded the Congregation of the Holy Family to serve broken families, the sick, and the dying. Despite facing misunderstanding and opposition, she persevered in her mission.
prayer: My God, let me suffer and love.

name: Mariana de Jesús
tagline: Ecuadorian mystic known for her self-sacrifice during a plague and earthquake.
description: St. Mariana de Jesús, born in Quito, Ecuador, dedicated her life to prayer and selflessness in the face of communal suffering. During horrific plagues and earthquakes, she offered her life for the well-being of her fellow citizens, embodying profound love and devotion. Her mystical experiences and commitment to God have made her a beloved figure in her homeland.
prayer: Lord, I offer my life for the cessation of these calamities.

name: Marianne Cope
tagline: A German-American Franciscan sister who continued St. Damien's work among the lepers of Molokai for over 30 years without ever contracting the disease.
description: St. Marianne Cope was a German-born American Franciscan sister who arrived in Hawaii in 1883 to manage hospitals and schools. After St. Damien's death, she took over the care of the Molokai leper settlement, serving for over 30 years. Remarkably, she never contracted the disease despite constant close contact.
prayer: I am not afraid of any disease.

name: Mark the Evangelist
tagline: St. Mark is celebrated for authoring the Gospel of Mark and serving as a close companion to the Apostle Peter.
description: St. Mark the Evangelist is one of the four Gospel writers of the New Testament, providing a vital account of Jesus’ life and teachings through his Gospel. He is also recognized as the founder of the Church of Alexandria, which became a significant center of Christianity. His feast is celebrated on April 25, a day marking his contributions to the faith and his enduring legacy through his writings.
prayer: The time has come, the Kingdom of God has come near

name: Maroun
tagline: A 5th-century hermit whose followers founded the Maronite Church, the largest Christian community in Lebanon.
description: St. Maroun was a hermit monk who lived on a mountain in Syria. He was renowned for his healing gifts and spiritual counsel, attracting many followers. After his death, his disciples formed a distinct community that would become the Maronite Church, which remains the spiritual heart of Lebanese Christianity.
prayer: The mountain is my cathedral.

name: Martha
tagline: Sister of Mary and Lazarus, known for her service and hospitality towards Jesus.
description: St. Martha is known for her unwavering faith and commitment to serving Jesus and her family. As the sister of Mary and Lazarus, she welcomed Christ into her home and displayed deep devotion amidst her busy life. Her character exemplifies the value of service and hospitality in the Christian faith.
prayer: You should not be troubled, for He is the one who can awaken the dead.

name: Martial
tagline: He is known for being one of the first bishops of Limoges and for his role in establishing and spreading Christianity in the region.
description: St. Martial was a bishop in Limoges who played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in the region of Aquitaine during the 3rd century. He is recognized for his unwavering faith and dedication to preaching the Gospel, despite facing persecution and hardship. His legacy of leadership and commitment to God’s work continues to inspire many believers.
prayer: Faith is the light that guides us through the darkness of doubt.

name: Martin de Porres
tagline: A devoted Dominican lay brother known for his profound compassion and extraordinary healing abilities.
description: St. Martin de Porres was born in Lima, Peru, to a Spanish father and a black mother, and he faced racial discrimination throughout his life. He joined the Dominicans as a lay brother, where he dedicated his life to serving the poor and caring for the sick, including both people and animals. His legacy of charity and humility continues to inspire those who seek to promote racial harmony and health care for all.
prayer: No one makes a greater mistake than he who did nothing because he could do only a little.

name: Martin I
tagline: He is known for his steadfast resistance against the Monothelite heresy.
description: St. Martin I served as pope in the 7th century and is remembered for his courageous stand against the Monothelite doctrine, which claimed that Christ had only one will. His commitment to faith led to his imprisonment and exile by the Byzantine Emperor. His martyrdom and dedication have made him a revered figure in the Catholic Church.
prayer: The church must be free.

name: Martin of Tours
tagline: A soldier who became a compassionate bishop known for his acts of charity.
description: St. Martin of Tours was born into a Roman military family in what is now Hungary. He famously tore his military cloak in two to share with a beggar during a snowstorm, a gesture that would define his life as one of charity and leadership. Later, he became the Bishop of Tours and played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in Gaul.
prayer: I am a soldier of Christ, I cannot fight.

name: Mary MacKillop
tagline: Pioneer of Catholic education in Australia and founder of the Sisters of St. Joseph.
description: St. Mary MacKillop was the first Australian to be canonized as a saint in the Catholic Church. She dedicated her life to educating the underprivileged, particularly the poor and Aboriginal children, often overcoming significant challenges. Her legacy is celebrated through the continued work of the Sisters of St. Joseph across Australia and beyond.
prayer: If you have a good spirit, you will inspire hope in others.

name: Mary Magdalene
tagline: The first witness to the Resurrection of Jesus and a devoted follower.
description: St. Mary Magdalene is celebrated as a pivotal figure in Christianity, known for her unwavering support of Jesus throughout His ministry. She uniquely witnessed His crucifixion and was the first to encounter the resurrected Christ, tasked with sharing the good news with the apostles. Her life reflects transformation, faith, and forgiveness, inspiring countless believers to follow her example of devotion.
prayer: I have seen the Lord.

name: Mary of Egypt
tagline: A 5th-century penitent who spent 47 years in the desert doing penance after a life of sin in Alexandria.
description: St. Mary of Egypt lived as a prostitute in Alexandria for 17 years before experiencing a dramatic conversion while trying to enter the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. She spent the remaining 47 years of her life as a hermit in the Jordanian desert, living on herbs and divine grace.
prayer: An invisible force held me back at the door of the church.

name: Mary, Mother of God
tagline: Being the mother of Jesus Christ and a central figure in Christianity.
description: St. Mary is revered as the mother of Jesus Christ, embodying grace and faith. Her acceptance of God’s will makes her a profound example for all Christians, highlighting the importance of trust in divine purpose. She holds a unique position within the Catholic Church, venerated not only for her maternal role but also for her unwavering devotion to God.
prayer: My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord

name: Matilda of Ringelheim
tagline: A German queen renowned for her generosity to the poor and her founding of monasteries and charitable institutions.
description: St. Matilda was the wife of King Henry I of Germany (Henry the Fowler) and mother of Emperor Otto the Great. After her husband's death, she devoted her wealth to founding monasteries, convents, and charitable institutions. Despite being criticized by her sons for her generosity, she continued her charitable work throughout her life.
prayer: The riches of this world mean nothing compared to the treasures of heaven.

name: Matrona of Moscow
tagline: A blind and crippled Russian wonderworker who was one of the most beloved saints of the 20th century.
description: Born blind in a peasant family, Matrona spent her life in prayer and counseling thousands who sought her help during the difficult years of Soviet rule. Despite her physical disabilities and the constant threat of arrest, she was a source of spiritual light and healing for any who came to her.
prayer: Come to me and tell me as if I were alive, and I will see you and hear you, and help you.

name: Matthew
tagline: St. Matthew is recognized as one of the twelve Apostles and the author of the Gospel of Matthew.
description: St. Matthew, originally a tax collector, was called by Jesus to be one of His disciples, showcasing the transformative power of grace. After the Ascension of Jesus, he dedicated his life to spreading the Gospel, traveling to various regions to preach. His Gospel is notable for its focus on the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecies, making it a vital text for Christians.
prayer: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

name: Matthias
tagline: Chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot as one of the Twelve Apostles.
description: St. Matthias is renowned for his unwavering faith, having been selected as an apostle shortly after the Ascension of Christ. His commitment to spreading the gospel and serving the early Church exemplifies the virtues of obedience and perseverance. Despite his lesser-known status among the apostles, Matthias's role was pivotal in maintaining the integrity of the Twelve.
prayer: It is necessary that one become a witness of the resurrection.

name: Maurice
tagline: Maurice is known as a leader of the Theban Legion and a martyr under the Roman Empire.
description: St. Maurice was an early Christian martyr and the commander of the Theban Legion in the Roman army. Refusing to participate in pagan sacrifices, he and his fellow soldiers faced execution for their faith. Maurice's steadfastness and leadership in the face of persecution made him a beloved figure and a symbol of military obedience to Christ.
prayer: The enemy does not attack when he knows the victor to be ever watchful.

name: Maurus
tagline: Maurus was a Benedictine monk and is known for being the first disciple of St. Benedict.
description: St. Maurus was born in Italy and became a follower of St. Benedict at the famous monastery of Monte Cassino. He is noted for his role in shaping monastic life and traditions in early Christianity. His commitment to the Benedictine Rule exemplified the values of prayer, work, and community.
prayer: It is better to make mistakes in kindness than to work miracles in unkindness.

name: Maximilian Kolbe
tagline: Knight of the Immaculata
description: St. Maximilian Kolbe was a Franciscan friar who volunteered to die in place of a stranger at Auschwitz. A pioneer of Catholic media and devotion to Mary, he showed that the greatest love is laying down one's life for another.
prayer: The most deadly poison of our times is indifference. Let us not be indifferent.

name: Maximilian of Tebessa
tagline: Being a Christian martyr during the Roman Empire and known for his bold confession of faith.
description: St. Maximilian was a young Christian from Tebessa in present-day Algeria, who boldly professed his faith in the face of persecution. He was a member of a prominent family and chose martyrdom over renouncing his beliefs, ultimately executed for refusing military service against fellow Christians. His story serves as a testament to the power of conviction and the sacrifices made for the faith in its early days.
prayer: I am a Christian, and I cannot serve the idols.

name: Maximinus of Aix
tagline: He was the first bishop of Aix-en-Provence and played a key role in spreading Christianity in the region.
description: St. Maximinus of Aix is remembered as a devoted leader of the early Church in Provence, tirelessly working to convert and support his community. His efforts laid the groundwork for the growth of the Christian faith in southern France during a time of significant persecution. He is venerated not only for his ministry but also for his wisdom and guidance to his followers.
prayer: Faith is the foundation upon which we build our lives.

name: Medard
tagline: He is known for his role as a bishop and protector against storms, particularly in the region of Picardy, France.
description: St. Medard was a 6th-century bishop known for his piety and dedication to God. He became famous as a protector against storms and was often sought for his intercessions for good weather. His charitable work and commitment to the spiritual welfare of his people made him a beloved figure in the Church.
prayer: Faith is the light that guides us through the darkest storms.

name: Mesrop Mashtots
tagline: An Armenian monk who invented the Armenian alphabet to translate the Bible and preserve Armenian Christian culture.
description: St. Mesrop Mashtots was an Armenian monk, theologian, and linguist who created the Armenian alphabet around 405 AD. His invention allowed the Bible and liturgical texts to be translated into Armenian, preserving Armenian Christian identity and culture under foreign domination for centuries.
prayer: To know the letters is to know God's Word.

name: Methodius
tagline: Co-patron of the Slavic people, known for his missionary work alongside his brother Cyril.
description: St. Methodius was a 9th-century missionary known for bringing Christianity to the Slavic nations, particularly Great Moravia. Alongside his brother Cyril, he developed the Glagolitic alphabet, the first script used for writing Old Church Slavonic. Their work laid the foundation for Slavic culture and literacy.
prayer: Let us, therefore, accept the teachings of Holy Scripture.

name: Michael de los Santos
tagline: He is known for his dedication to the missions in the American territories.
description: St. Michael de los Santos was a Spanish priest who became a Franciscan missionary in the Philippines. He was known for his tireless work in spreading the Christian faith among the indigenous people. His life was marked by a deep commitment to his faith and an unwavering spirit of service.
prayer: Preach the Gospel at all times

name: Michael McGivney
tagline: Founder of the Knights of Columbus to support Catholic families.
description: Blessed Michael McGivney was an American priest dedicated to serving his parish and empowering families through social welfare. As the founder of the Knights of Columbus in 1882, he pioneered an organization that provided assistance to families in need during an era of hardship. His legacy continues to inspire charitable work and community service in the Catholic Church today.
prayer: The greatest thing that we must remember is that we are part of the great family of God.

name: Michael the Archangel
tagline: St. Michael is revered as the archangel who leads the heavenly army against the forces of evil.
description: St. Michael the Archangel is a central figure in Christian tradition, symbolizing divine protection and strength. He is often depicted as a majestic warrior with a sword, defeating the devil and safeguarding souls. His role as a protector of the faithful has made him a beloved saint across various cultures.
prayer: Who is like God?

name: Miguel Pro
tagline: A Mexican Jesuit priest known for his courageous ministry and martyrdom during a time of intense religious persecution.
description: Blessed Miguel Pro was a Mexican Jesuit priest renowned for his willingness to serve others during a brutal religious crackdown in Mexico. Utilizing disguises, he secretly provided sacraments and support to those in need, ultimately leading to his arrest and martyrdom. He was executed in 1927, proclaiming his faith with the words 'Viva Cristo Rey!' as a testament to his unwavering dedication to Christ.
prayer: Viva Cristo Rey! (Long live Christ the King!)

name: Monica
tagline: She is celebrated as the mother of St. Augustine, who underwent a remarkable conversion due in large part to her persistent prayers.
description: St. Monica was a woman of profound faith and unwavering resolve, dedicated to the conversion of her wayward son, Augustine. Through years of heartfelt prayers and patience, she witnessed his transformation into one of the Church's greatest saints. Her life story exemplifies the power of maternal love and the importance of hope in times of struggle.
prayer: Nothing is far from God.

name: Moses the Black
tagline: A former Ethiopian gang leader and robber who converted to Christianity and became one of the greatest Desert Fathers.
description: St. Moses the Black was an Ethiopian servant dismissed for theft who became the leader of a gang of bandits. After hiding from authorities in a desert monastery, he was so moved by the monks' way of life that he converted and became a monk himself, eventually leading 75 disciples.
prayer: Go, sit in your cell, and your cell will teach you everything.

name: Mother Teresa
tagline: Saint of the Gutters
description: St. Mother Teresa of Calcutta saw the face of Christ in the poorest of the poor. She founded the Missionaries of Charity and spent decades serving the dying and destitute in Kolkata, even while experiencing a prolonged dark night of the soul.
prayer: If you judge people, you have no time to love them. Spread love everywhere you go. Let no one ever come to you without leaving happier.

name: Narcisa de Jesús
tagline: An Ecuadorian laywoman known for her extreme penances, deep prayer life, and mystical experiences.
description: St. Narcisa de Jesús Martillo Morán was an Ecuadorian laywoman who lived a life of extraordinary penance and prayer. Though she never joined a religious order, she lived as a consecrated laywoman, spending her days in prayer, fasting, and works of charity. She died in Lima, Peru, at the age of 36.
prayer: My only desire is to love God above all things.

name: Nektarios of Aegina
tagline: A Greek Orthodox bishop who was unjustly exiled and slandered, yet responded with humility and built a convent on the island of Aegina.
description: St. Nektarios was a Greek Orthodox bishop who was falsely accused of corruption and stripped of his position. Rather than fight back, he accepted his disgrace with humility and devoted himself to writing, teaching, and building the Holy Trinity Convent on the island of Aegina. He is one of the most beloved modern Greek saints.
prayer: Love all people equally.

name: Nemesius
tagline: He is known for his contributions to early Christian theology and his defense of the faith against heresies.
description: St. Nemesius was an influential bishop from the early Christian period who played a vital role in the theological debates of his time. Renowned for his writings, he sought to clarify the divine nature of Christ and the Holy Spirit. His legacy continues to inspire scholars and theologians striving for truth in their faith.
prayer: Faith is the light that illuminates the path of truth.

name: Nicetas of Remesiana
tagline: He was known for his evangelization efforts among the Goths and for his theological writings.
description: St. Nicetas of Remesiana was a Bishop in the early Church who played a crucial role in spreading Christianity among the Gothic tribes. He is credited with composing various theological texts that aided the understanding of the faith in a time of great cultural upheaval. His dedication to the pastoral care of his flock and commitment to missionary work helped lay the groundwork for the future growth of the Church in Eastern Europe.
prayer: Faith is the anchor of the soul.

name: Nicholas
tagline: A beloved bishop renowned for his acts of charity and compassion.
description: St. Nicholas, the Bishop of Myra, was known for his unwavering generosity and dedication to serving the needy. His legendary deeds of secret gift-giving laid the foundation for modern traditions of Santa Claus. Celebrated for his compassion, he is a beloved figure among Christians, deeply revered in both Western and Eastern traditions.
prayer: I will not let my hand fall away from what I serve.

name: Nicholas of Myra
tagline: He is renowned for his acts of charity and generosity towards the poor and for performing miracles.
description: St. Nicholas of Myra was a 4th-century bishop known for his secret gift-giving, which laid the groundwork for the modern Santa Claus tradition. His life was marked by compassion, especially towards children and the less fortunate. He became famous for several miracles attributed to him, including saving sailors and providing dowries for poor girls.
prayer: It is better to give than to receive.

name: Nicholas of Toledo
tagline: Nicholas of Toledo is celebrated for his contributions to the church and his moral integrity.
description: St. Nicholas of Toledo was a noted 12th-century Spanish priest known for his dedication to pastoral care. Throughout his life, he demonstrated remarkable compassion towards the sick and the needy, earning the respect and love of his community. He is remembered as a man of great faith and wisdom, whose teachings continue to inspire many in the Catholic tradition.
prayer: Faith is like a grain of mustard seed

name: Nicholas Owen
tagline: Nicholas Owen was a Jesuit priest and martyr known for his role in the English Catholic underground.
description: St. Nicholas Owen was a devoted layman and carpenter who worked tirelessly to support the work of the Jesuit missionaries in England. His remarkable skill in building hiding places for priests led to his eventual arrest and torture. Ultimately, he gave his life for the faith, becoming a symbol of courage and loyalty in the face of persecution.
prayer: The dignity of man is a divine quality.

name: Nina Martyr of Georgia
tagline: A teenage Georgian girl martyred in the Soviet purges for refusing to remove her cross and deny Christ.
description: St. Nina was a young Georgian Christian woman who was arrested during Stalin's Great Purge for her religious activities. She was ordered to renounce her faith and remove her cross necklace. When she refused, she was tortured and executed. She was glorified as a new martyr by the Georgian Orthodox Church.
prayer: I cannot remove my cross.

name: Nino of Georgia
tagline: The 'Enlightener of Georgia' who brought Christianity to the ancient kingdom of Iberia (modern Georgia) in the 4th century.
description: St. Nino was a young woman from Cappadocia who traveled to the ancient kingdom of Iberia (modern Georgia) as a captive or pilgrim. Through her prayers and miracles, she converted Queen Nana and eventually King Mirian III, leading to the declaration of Christianity as the state religion. She is revered as equal to the apostles in the Georgian Orthodox Church.
prayer: Christ is the light of all nations.

name: Norbert
tagline: He founded the Premonstratensian order and devoted his life to reforming others through deep holiness.
description: St. Norbert was born around 1080 in Xanten, Germany, and experienced a profound conversion after a near-death experience. Committed to reforming the clergy and promoting a communal monastic life, he founded the Premonstratensian order, emphasizing discipline and spiritual integrity. He played a pivotal role in advocating for peace during his lifetime and continued to inspire generations through his dedication to God and the Church.
prayer: The greatest tenderness of heart and the most fervent love of God are found in true priests.

name: Notburga
tagline: A Tyrolean peasant servant known for her charity to the poor and her defense of workers' right to rest on Sundays.
description: St. Notburga was a Tyrolean kitchen servant who gave leftover food to the poor against her employer's wishes. When fired, she worked for a farmer who agreed to let her attend Mass and rest on Sundays. According to legend, when he reneged on this promise, her sickle floated in the air, proving God's will for Sunday rest.
prayer: Give to the poor what belongs to God.

name: Odilo of Cluny
tagline: He is renowned for his role in the development of the monastic reform movement and the expansion of the Cluniac order.
description: St. Odilo of Cluny was a Benedictine monk who became the second abbot of Cluny Abbey. Under his leadership, the monastery flourished, and its influence expanded across Europe, promoting a return to strict monastic discipline and spirituality. He is also remembered for instituting the observance of All Souls' Day, emphasizing the importance of praying for the deceased.
prayer: We must strive to please others, but most importantly, we must please our God.

name: Olaf
tagline: St. Olaf was a king who played a crucial role in the Christianization of Norway.
description: St. Olaf, known for his fierce leadership, ascended to the throne of Norway in the 11th century. He was instrumental in spreading Christianity throughout the region, often through both peaceful evangelization and military means. Driven by his faith, he is remembered for his dedication to creating a united Christian kingdom.
prayer: Christ is my light

name: Olga of Kiev
tagline: The first Christian ruler of Kievan Rus', known for her wisdom and her role in paving the way for her grandson St. Vladimir.
description: Olga was a regent who ruled Kyivan Rus' with great skill. She was baptized in Constantinople and attempted to bring Christianity to her people, though her own son refused to convert. She is remembered as the first saint of the Russian Orthodox Church.
prayer: Let my people see the light of Christ.

name: Oliver Plunkett
tagline: St. Oliver Plunkett was a courageous archbishop and martyr during the persecution of Catholics in Ireland.
description: St. Oliver Plunkett was a prominent figure in the Catholic Church during a time of great turmoil in Ireland. He dedicated his life to serving the spiritual needs of his people, ultimately sacrificing his own life for his unwavering faith. His execution in 1681 made him a symbol of resistance against religious oppression and a celebrated martyr.
prayer: I die innocent of all charges against me.

name: Oscar Romero
tagline: Archbishop martyred for his defense of the poor and oppressed in El Salvador.
description: St. Oscar Romero was a prominent Salvadoran archbishop who spoke out against human rights abuses during the Salvadoran Civil War. Known for his unwavering commitment to social justice, he advocated for the vulnerable and marginalized in society. His life was tragically cut short when he was assassinated while celebrating Mass on March 24, 1980.
prayer: If we cannot see Christ in the poor, we cannot see him in the Eucharist.

name: Oswald
tagline: Oswald is recognized for his martyrdom and dedication to the faith.
description: St. Oswald was a king of Northumbria who played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity in his region. He was known for his deep faith and his commitment to fostering peace and justice. After his martyrdom, he became a venerated saint, influencing many through his exemplary life and sacrifice.
prayer: As long as I live, I will continue to speak of God's love.

name: Oswald of Northumbria
tagline: He is known for his efforts in spreading Christianity in Northumbria.
description: St. Oswald was an influential king of Northumbria who played a crucial role in the Christianization of England. He established a strong alliance with the Irish Church, which helped to promote the faith among his people. His reign was marked by notable victories and the founding of monasteries that contributed to the spiritual growth of the region.
prayer: Lord, I ask you to bless this nation and all who dwell within it.

name: Our Lady of Guadalupe
tagline: A prominent figure in Catholicism, she is known for her miraculous appearance to St. Juan Diego in Mexico.
description: Our Lady of Guadalupe is a significant figure in Catholic faith, celebrated for her apparitions to the indigenous Juan Diego in 1531. Her image, which appeared on his cloak, became a symbol of faith and unity for the Mexican people and beyond. She is revered as the Mother of the Americas, promoting love, compassion, and respect for life.
prayer: I am your mother, and I desire that you go and tell all that I will do for them.

name: Our Lady of Lourdes
tagline: The apparitions of the Virgin Mary to St. Bernadette in Lourdes, France.
description: St. Our Lady of Lourdes appeared to a young girl named Bernadette Soubirous in a grotto near Lourdes, France, in 1858. During these apparitions, she identified herself as the Immaculate Conception and conveyed messages of prayer and penance. Lourdes has since become a major pilgrimage site known for miraculous healings and a place of devotion.
prayer: I cannot promise you happiness in this life, but I can promise you happiness in the next.

name: Our Lady of the Rosary
tagline: The celebration honors the Blessed Virgin Mary under her title of Our Lady of the Rosary.
description: Our Lady of the Rosary dates back to the 13th century, reflecting the importance of the rosary in Catholic devotion. She is seen as a powerful intercessor and has inspired countless faithful to seek her guidance through prayer. The feast emphasizes the role of Mary in the church and the spiritual strength of the rosary.
prayer: The rosary is a powerful weapon to put the demons to flight and to keep oneself free from sin.

name: Pachomius
tagline: The founder of 'cenobitic' (community) monasticism.
description: A former Roman soldier, Pachomius sought a way for monks to live together in community rather than as hermits. He wrote the first monastic Rule, emphasizing obedience, labor, and mutual support.
prayer: True virtue consists in doing God's will with a joyful heart.

name: Pacian of Barcelona
tagline: He was a bishop known for his theological writings and defense of Christian doctrine.
description: St. Pacian was a prominent bishop in the late 4th century, recognized for his strong stance against heresy and his efforts to win back lapsed Christians. He authored several letters and treatises that defended the importance of the sacraments and the need for moral purity among the faithful. His influence extended beyond his diocese, as he was consulted by other bishops on matters of doctrine and church governance.
prayer: We do not lose sight of heaven

name: Pacificus of San Severino
tagline: He is known for his deep spirituality and commitment to prayer and penance.
description: St. Pacificus of San Severino was an Italian Franciscan friar who dedicated his life to serving the poor and spreading the Gospel. Throughout his life, he engaged in rigorous self-discipline and promoted a deep devotion to prayer among his fellow friars. His legacy continues to inspire those who seek a life of humility and service in their communities.
prayer: In every act of kindness, God is present.

name: Padre Pio
tagline: Bearer of the Wounds
description: St. Padre Pio was a Capuchin friar who bore the stigmata for 50 years. Known for his gift of reading souls in confession, bilocation, and healing, he endured immense suffering with patience and devotion. Millions sought his counsel and intercession.
prayer: Pray, hope, and don't worry. Worry is useless. God is merciful and will hear your prayer.

name: Paisios of Mount Athos
tagline: A modern Athonite elder known for his profound spiritual wisdom and prophecies.
description: Paisios was an Athonite monk who became world-famous in his later years. Thousands of people flocked to his small cell on Mount Athos for advice. He was known for his extreme asceticism, his sense of humor, and his ability to see the spiritual root of people's modern psychological struggles.
prayer: God is the only one who can fill the void in a person's life.

name: Pammachius
tagline: St. Pammachius is known for being a dedicated Christian martyr and an advocate for the needy during the early days of Christianity.
description: St. Pammachius was a prominent Roman noble who became a Christian martyr during the persecution of Christians in the early church. Known for his unwavering faith and commitment to aiding the poor and sick, he was a close confidante of St. Jerome, who praised his virtues and dedication to the faith. He ultimately died for his beliefs, leaving behind a legacy of charity and devotion that continues to inspire the faithful.
prayer: The blood of martyrs is the seed of the Church.

name: Pantaleon
tagline: St. Pantaleon is known as a physician and martyr who devoted his life to healing and serving others.
description: St. Pantaleon, a physician in the fourth century, became renowned for his miraculous healings through faith. After converting to Christianity, he refused to renounce his faith even under persecution, leading to his martyrdom. His legacy of compassion and dedication to the sick continues to inspire medical professionals today.
prayer: The physician should be aware that the greatest skill of healing is prayer.

name: Paschal Baylón
tagline: He is known for his deep devotion to the Eucharist and for his role as a Franciscan friar.
description: St. Paschal Baylón was a Spanish Franciscan who dedicated his life to serving the poor and promoting devotion to the Holy Eucharist. He is remembered for his piety and his efforts in the reform of the Franciscan order. His dedication and humility made him a beloved figure in the Church, inspiring many to a greater love for the sacrament.
prayer: The Eucharist is the greatest gift of God to us.

name: Patrick
tagline: St. Patrick is renowned for bringing Christianity to Ireland and using the shamrock to explain the Holy Trinity.
description: A bishop and missionary, St. Patrick played a crucial role in converting the Irish to Christianity during the 5th century. According to legend, he drove snakes out of Ireland, symbolizing the eradication of paganism. His teachings and use of everyday symbols made the Christian faith more accessible to the Irish people.
prayer: Be still and know that I am God.

name: Paul
tagline: A key figure in the early Christian church who spread the Gospel to the Gentiles.
description: St. Paul, originally known as Saul of Tarsus, was a zealous persecutor of Christians before experiencing a profound conversion on the road to Damascus. He became one of Christianity's most influential apostles, traveling extensively to establish churches and writing letters that form a significant portion of the New Testament. His theological insights and teachings continue to shape Christian doctrine and practice today.
prayer: I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.

name: Paul Chong Hasang
tagline: A Korean lay catechist and seminarist martyred for his faith during the Joseon Dynasty persecutions.
description: St. Paul Chong Hasang was a Korean lay catechist whose father was one of the first Korean martyrs. He worked tirelessly to bring foreign missionaries into Korea and to organize the underground Catholic community. He was arrested, imprisoned, and eventually executed for his faith.
prayer: Even if we die, we cannot betray the Lord of heaven whom we serve.

name: Paul Miki
tagline: A Japanese Jesuit seminarian and one of the Twenty-Six Martyrs crucified in Nagasaki during the persecution of Christians.
description: St. Paul Miki was a Japanese Jesuit scholastic from a wealthy family who was one of the Twenty-Six Martyrs of Japan. He was arrested during the persecution under Toyotomi Hideyoshi and forced to march 600 miles to Nagasaki in winter. He preached his most powerful sermon from the cross before being killed by lance thrusts.
prayer: I have been living as a Japanese and I am dying as a Japanese. This land of mine is the cradle for Christianity.

name: Paul of the Cross
tagline: Founder of the Passionists, a religious order dedicated to the Passion of Christ.
description: St. Paul of the Cross was born in Italy and spent much of his life preaching and spreading devotion to the Passion of Jesus. He founded the Congregation of the Passion (the Passionists) to foster a deeper understanding of Christ's suffering. His profound spirituality and emphasis on contemplative prayer have inspired countless followers to deepen their faith.
prayer: May the Passion of Christ be always in our hearts.

name: Paul the Apostle
tagline: One of the most important figures in early Christianity and author of several New Testament letters.
description: St. Paul, originally known as Saul of Tarsus, experienced a dramatic conversion to Christianity on the road to Damascus. He dedicated his life to spreading the Gospel, establishing churches, and mentoring early Christians. His epistles remain foundational texts for Christian theology and practice.
prayer: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor demons, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers.

name: Paul the Simple
tagline: A hermit known for his deep spirituality and simple life of faith.
description: St. Paul the Simple was a hermit who embraced a life of solitude and prayer in the Egyptian desert. Renowned for his innocence and genuine faith, he became a model of simplicity in a world often filled with complexity. His life served as an inspiration to many, showcasing the profound richness found in a humble existence devoted to God.
prayer: The greatest action is not to act.

name: Pedro Calungsod
tagline: A Filipino teenage catechist who was martyred in Guam while defending a priest.
description: St. Pedro Calungsod was a devoted catechist who, at a young age, demonstrated remarkable dedication to his faith. His life was profoundly marked by his commitment to serving God and the Church, culminating in his martyrdom on the island of Guam. He is remembered not just for his courage, but also for inspiring young people to embrace their faith with zeal.
prayer: I will always be ready to lay down my life for the Lord and His mission.

name: Pelagia
tagline: Known for her conversion from a life of sin to a life dedicated to God.
description: St. Pelagia was originally a beautiful actress who lived a life of luxury and indulgence in Antioch. After hearing a sermon on repentance, she chose to abandon her former life and dedicated herself to prayer and penance. Her remarkable transformation inspires many to seek forgiveness and live a holy life.
prayer: The time is now to take up the cross and follow Him.

name: Peregrine Laziosi
tagline: He is renowned for his miraculous healing from cancer.
description: St. Peregrine Laziosi was a 14th-century Italian saint known for his deep faith and miraculous cures. After suffering from cancer himself, he experienced a profound healing through prayer and devotion, which inspired many to seek his intercession. He became a beloved figure, advocating for the sick and marginalized in society.
prayer: Where there is charity and wisdom, there is neither fear nor ignorance.

name: Perfectus
tagline: St. Perfectus is recognized as one of the early martyrs of the Christian faith during the Roman Empire.
description: St. Perfectus was a devoted Christian who boldly proclaimed his faith in a time of intense persecution. He became a martyr for his beliefs, inspiring countless others to hold fast to their faith. His legacy endures as a symbol of courage and resilience in the face of adversity.
prayer: Faith is the light that guides us through the darkness.

name: Perpetua
tagline: A young noblewoman and mother who kept a diary of her imprisonment and was martyred in Carthage for refusing to renounce her faith.
description: St. Perpetua was a young, well-educated noblewoman from Carthage who was arrested during the persecution of Emperor Septimius Severus. Despite her father's pleas and her love for her infant son, she refused to renounce her faith. Her prison diary is one of the earliest known writings by a Christian woman and provides a vivid account of early Christian martyrdom.
prayer: I am a Christian, and I cannot be called by any other name.

name: Peter
tagline: St. Peter is recognized as the first pope and a leader among the apostles.
description: Born as Simon in Galilee, he was a fisherman before becoming a devoted follower of Jesus Christ. Peter played a crucial role in the early Church, ultimately facing martyrdom in Rome for his steadfast faith. His legacy as the first pope and his role in spreading Christianity have made him a pillar of the Catholic Church.
prayer: You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.

name: Peter Canisius
tagline: A prominent figure in the Counter-Reformation and a Jesuit Doctor of the Church.
description: St. Peter Canisius was a pivotal figure in the Catholic Reformation in Germany, known for his fervent missionary work and his dedication to education. He authored influential catechisms that helped clarify Catholic doctrine during a time of great turmoil. His commitment to spreading the faith and his intellectual contributions earned him a place among the Doctors of the Church.
prayer: I have my own life to live and I must live it for God.

name: Peter Chanel
tagline: A Marist missionary who was martyred in Oceania while spreading the Christian faith.
description: St. Peter Chanel was a French priest who devoted his life to missionary work in the islands of Oceania. He faced great dangers but remained unwavering in his commitment to spreading Christianity. His efforts ultimately led to his martyrdom in 1841, affirming his legacy as a courageous missionary.
prayer: I do not fear death. I fear to die without having given myself completely to God.

name: Peter Claver
tagline: He is known for his dedicated work in serving African slaves in Colombia.
description: St. Peter Claver was a Spanish Jesuit priest who dedicated his life to the service of the enslaved people brought to the Americas. He is remembered for his compassion, providing care, and spreading the Christian faith among the African slaves. Claver baptized more than 300,000 slaves throughout his life, earning him the title 'Apostle of the Negroes.'
prayer: It is not enough to love the negro

name: Peter Damian
tagline: He was a prominent reformer of the Church and an advocate for clerical celibacy.
description: St. Peter Damian was a Benedictine monk and a cardinal who played a critical role in the reform of the clergy during the 11th century. He was known for his intense spirituality and his dedication to God, earning him the title of Doctor of the Church. His writings emphasized the importance of purity and the need for reform within the Church, making him an influential figure in his time.
prayer: Be who you are and be that well.

name: Peter Julian Eymard
tagline: He is revered as the Apostle of the Eucharist and founded the Blessed Sacrament Fathers.
description: Born in France, St. Peter Julian Eymard dedicated his life to promoting devotion to the Eucharist. He founded the Congregation of the Blessed Sacrament to foster Eucharistic worship and ensure that the presence of Christ in the Eucharist was honored and celebrated. His teachings and writings continue to inspire countless faithful in their spiritual journeys.
prayer: The Eucharist is the bread of life, the source of all grace.

name: Peter of Alcántara
tagline: A Spanish Franciscan mystic known for his intense commitment to penance and spiritual guidance, particularly in his support of St. Teresa of Ávila.
description: St. Peter of Alcántara was a dedicated Franciscan who exemplified the life of deep contemplation and penitential practices. He played a significant role in the reform of the Franciscan Order alongside St. Teresa of Ávila, encouraging a return to strict observance. His teachings and spiritual writings continue to inspire those seeking a deeper relationship with God through prayer and asceticism.
prayer: The soul that takes for its guide the Spirit of God will never be deceived.

name: Peter To Rot
tagline: A Papuan catechist who was martyred by the Japanese during World War II for defending the sanctity of Christian marriage.
description: St. Peter To Rot was a catechist from the Tolai people of Papua New Guinea. During the Japanese occupation in World War II, he continued to lead his community in prayer and defended the sanctity of Christian marriage against the occupiers' attempts to impose polygamy. He was arrested and killed by lethal injection.
prayer: I must fulfill my duty as a catechist.

name: Philip Neri
tagline: The Apostle of Joy
description: St. Philip Neri was the joyful heart of Counter-Reformation Rome. Known for his humor, pranks, and ecstatic prayer, he founded the Oratory and drew people to God through laughter and friendship. His heart literally enlarged from the force of divine love.
prayer: A joyful heart is more easily made perfect than a downcast one. Cheerfulness strengthens the heart and helps us persevere.

name: Philip the Apostle
tagline: One of the Twelve Apostles who was instrumental in bringing others to Jesus.
description: St. Philip the Apostle is remembered for his role in the early ministry of Jesus Christ and for bringing Nathanael to Him. He actively preached the Gospel in Asia Minor and is recognized for his commitment to evangelization. His direct inquiries to Jesus reveal a sincere seeker of truth and understanding.
prayer: Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us.

name: Pier Giorgio Frassati
tagline: A compassionate young Italian known for serving the poor while passionately engaging in athletics and mountaineering.
description: Blessed Pier Giorgio Frassati was a remarkable Italian youth who dedicated his life to serving the underprivileged, often reflecting his deep Catholic faith through acts of charity. Despite his love for sports and the outdoors, he maintained a strong commitment to social reform and community service. His life, cut short at 24, continues to inspire young Catholics to embrace both faith and action in their lives.
prayer: The world is in great need of people who can awaken hope.

name: Pius V
tagline: Pope who excommunicated Queen Elizabeth I and established the Tridentine Mass.
description: St. Pius V was a reformist pope known for his commitment to the Council of Trent's decrees, which sought to address issues within the Church. He is most renowned for promulgating the Roman Missal, which standardized the Mass throughout the Catholic Church. His papacy was marked by significant efforts to strengthen the Catholic faith in the face of the Reformation.
prayer: All the good works in the world will not save us without faith.

name: Pius X
tagline: St. Pius X was a Pope renowned for promoting early Communion for children and reforming liturgical practices.
description: Born in Riese, Italy, St. Pius X served as Pope from 1903 until his death in 1914, leading significant reforms in the Church. His advocacy for the reception of Holy Communion at an early age transformed the spiritual lives of many children. St. Pius X is remembered for his humble demeanor, strong leadership, and dedication to restoring the Church's focus on the Eucharist.
prayer: Holy Communion is the shortest and safest way to Heaven.

name: Polycarp
tagline: An early Christian bishop and martyr, Polycarp was a direct disciple of St. John the Apostle.
description: St. Polycarp served as the Bishop of Smyrna and was renowned for his unwavering faith amidst persecution. At the age of 86, he faced martyrdom with remarkable courage, famously refusing to renounce his faith. His legacy is celebrated by the early Church and remains an inspiration for many believers today.
prayer: Eighty-six years have I served Him, and He has done me no wrong. How can I blaspheme my King and Savior?

name: Rabanus Maurus
tagline: A Carolingian-era Benedictine monk, archbishop, and scholar known as 'the Teacher of Germany' for his encyclopedic works.
description: St. Rabanus Maurus was a Frankish Benedictine monk who became Archbishop of Mainz. He was one of the most important scholars of the Carolingian Renaissance, writing encyclopedias, biblical commentaries, and the famous hymn 'Veni Creator Spiritus.' He earned the title 'Praeceptor Germaniae' (Teacher of Germany).
prayer: Come, Holy Spirit, Creator blest.

name: Rafqa
tagline: A Lebanese Maronite nun who voluntarily asked God for suffering and endured blindness and crippling pain with extraordinary joy.
description: St. Rafqa (Rebecca) was a Lebanese Maronite nun who, after years of teaching and religious life, prayed to share in the sufferings of Christ. She soon went blind and became paralyzed, enduring 29 years of intense suffering with remarkable joy and patience. She was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI in 2001.
prayer: I asked my Lord for suffering and He gave it to me abundantly.

name: Raphael the Archangel
tagline: The healing angel who guides Tobias in the Book of Tobit.
description: St. Raphael the Archangel is revered as one of the three archangels mentioned in sacred scripture. He plays a significant role in the Book of Tobit, where he aids Tobias on his journey and restores the sight of his father, Tobit. As a symbol of healing and guidance, St. Raphael inspires the faithful to trust in divine assistance during their struggles.
prayer: I am the angel Raphael

name: Raymond of Peñafort
tagline: He is known for his significant contributions to canon law and the establishment of the Order of Preachers.
description: St. Raymond of Peñafort was a renowned Spanish priest and Dominican friar who dedicated his life to the service of the Church. He is celebrated for compiling many of the Church's laws and for promoting the Sacrament of Confession. Revered for his wisdom and commitment to education, he also played a vital role in the Christianization of the Moors in Spain.
prayer: The greatest among you will be your servant.

name: Richard of Chichester
tagline: Richard was known for his strong leadership as Bishop of Chichester and his dedication to pastoral care.
description: St. Richard of Chichester was born into a noble family and later became a scholar at the University of Oxford. He was elected Bishop of Chichester and worked tirelessly to reform the church, emphasizing pastoral care for the faithful. His life was marked by a deep commitment to God, and he is remembered for his compassion and integrity.
prayer: Lord, I am willing to do whatever you wish.

name: Rita of Cascia
tagline: A devoted widow and nun who is recognized for her deep mystical spirituality and bearing the stigmata.
description: St. Rita of Cascia was born in Italy and lived a life marked by suffering and deep faith. After enduring a troubled marriage, she became a nun and dedicated herself to prayer and compassion for others. Known as the 'Saint of the Impossible', she inspires countless individuals facing dire situations to trust in God's mercy.
prayer: Pray to God, and He will hear you.

name: Robert Bellarmine
tagline: A prominent Jesuit cardinal and Doctor of the Church, recognized for his defense of Catholic doctrine.
description: St. Robert Bellarmine was a pivotal figure in the Counter-Reformation, known for his deep commitment to teaching and defending the faith. He served as a cardinal and was instrumental in shaping the Catholic Church’s response to Protestantism through his writings and theological insights. His legacy continues to inspire those involved in education and catechesis today.
prayer: The church is a great liar, and it lies against itself in order to unite itself.

name: Robert of Newminster
tagline: He is known for his role in the founding of the Cistercian order in the 12th century.
description: St. Robert of Newminster was an English Cistercian monk and the abbot of the monastery at Newminster. He became a significant figure in the monastic reform of his time, helping to establish communities that emphasized simplicity and prayer. His dedication to the Cistercian way of life inspired many others to follow his spiritual path.
prayer: The good man owes it to himself to be better than he is.

name: Roch
tagline: St. Roch is celebrated for his dedication to caring for plague victims, even at the cost of his own health.
description: Born into a noble family in France, St. Roch devoted his life to serving the sick and poor, particularly during times of plague. After contracting the disease himself, he was cared for by a dog that brought him food and companionship. His legacy as a healer and protector lives on, inspiring countless individuals to show compassion and care for others afflicted by illness.
prayer: I am but a servant of God.

name: Romanus of Condat
tagline: He is known for founding the Abbey of Condat and promoting a life of prayer and asceticism among monks.
description: St. Romanus of Condat was a revered hermit and abbot known for his commitment to monastic life in the wilderness of modern-day France. He founded the Abbey of Condat, where he emphasized the virtues of prayer, community, and asceticism, leading many souls to a deeper relationship with God. His life exemplified humility, faithfulness, and devotion, inspiring generations of monks and laypeople alike.
prayer: It is in solitude that we can truly discover God's presence.

name: Romuald
tagline: He founded the Camaldolese order and significantly reformed monastic life in the early medieval period.
description: St. Romuald was a pivotal figure in monastic reform during the 11th century, known for establishing the Camaldolese order, which emphasized solitude and contemplation. His life was marked by a deep commitment to prayer and the search for a more austere lifestyle, leading him to inspire countless others in their spiritual journey. Throughout his lifetime, Romuald's teachings promoted a return to the core values of monasticism, focusing on discipline and solitude.
prayer: In the same way that we care for the Church, so we must care for ourselves.

name: Roque González
tagline: A Jesuit missionary who founded several of the famous Guaraní Reductions in South America before being martyred.
description: St. Roque González de Santa Cruz was a Paraguayan Jesuit and one of the first criollo (American-born) priests in South America. He founded several Jesuit Reductions among the Guaraní people, creating self-sustaining communities. He was killed by a shaman who opposed Christian influence.
prayer: I came to bring the Gospel to the ends of the earth.

name: Rose of Lima
tagline: Known as the first indigenous saint of the Americas, St. Rose of Lima is celebrated for her deep spirituality and commitment to serving the poor.
description: Born Isabel Flores de Oliva in Lima, Peru, Rose adopted the name of a rose to express her beauty of spirit. Throughout her life, she dedicated herself to prayer, fasting, and helping those in need, often taking extreme measures of penance. Her dedication to God and the marginalized made her a beloved figure, and she was canonized in 1671, becoming the first saint of the Americas.
prayer: I am a servant of God and a servant of the poor.

name: Rose of Viterbo
tagline: A courageous young visionary who passionately preached for the faith and stood up against Emperor Frederick II.
description: St. Rose of Viterbo was a remarkable young woman known for her fervent preaching and commitment to the Christian faith. Born in Viterbo, Italy, she boldly challenged the political and religious authorities of her time. Her unwavering courage and deep devotion to Christ inspired many in her community, leaving a lasting legacy as a champion of faith.
prayer: I am the servant of the Lord, may it be done to me according to Your word.

name: Rose Philippine Duchesne
tagline: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne was a pioneering missionary who played a significant role in the education of Native Americans in the United States.
description: Born in France, St. Rose Philippine Duchesne felt a calling to serve as a missionary in America, where she dedicated her life to education and the spiritual nourishment of Native American communities. Overcoming great challenges, she founded schools and spread the teachings of Christ among those she served. Her unwavering faith and compassion have made her a beloved figure in the Catholic Church.
prayer: I wish to be like the good Mother who offered her son on the altar for the sake of souls.

name: Rufinus
tagline: Rufinus is venerated as a martyr and saint who died for his faith during the early Christian persecutions.
description: St. Rufinus was a devoted Christian who faced persecution for his beliefs in the early 4th century. He exemplified courage in the face of adversity and ultimately gave his life for his faith. His legacy continues to inspire Christians to stand firm in their convictions.
prayer: Faith is to believe what you do not see

name: Rupert of Salzburg
tagline: He is known for founding the Diocese of Salzburg and spreading Christianity in the region.
description: St. Rupert, the first bishop of Salzburg, is celebrated for his missionary work in the 8th century. He founded the Abbey of St. Peter in Salzburg, which became a center of learning and culture. His influence helped to establish Christianity in the Alpine region, making him a key figure in the spread of the faith in Central Europe.
prayer: Christ is our peace, and in Him we are saved.

name: Sabina
tagline: St. Sabina is known for her martyrdom and her unwavering faith in the face of persecution.
description: St. Sabina was a noble Roman woman who embraced Christianity and was martyred for her faith. She is celebrated for her steadfastness in belief, especially during the persecutions against Christians. Her virtues of courage and faith have inspired many in their spiritual journeys.
prayer: The glory of God is the living man, and the life of man is the vision of God.

name: Saturninus
tagline: He is known for being one of the early bishops of Toulouse and a martyr for the faith.
description: St. Saturninus was a prominent early Christian leader in Toulouse, known for his unwavering faith during a time of great persecution. According to tradition, he was martyred for refusing to renounce Christianity, highlighting his dedication to God. His legacy has continued to inspire many believers throughout the centuries.
prayer: The power of Christ compels me to speak the truth.

name: Savva of Serbia
tagline: The first Archbishop of the autocephalous Serbian Orthodox Church and national hero of Serbia.
description: Savva was a prince who secretly fled to Mount Athos to become a monk. He later returned to Serbia to establish its independent church, founded schools and hospitals, and negotiated peace between his brothers. He is considered the father of Serbian culture and identity.
prayer: The soul is more precious than the body.

name: Scholastica
tagline: Lifelong dedication to monastic life and influence on the Benedictine order.
description: St. Scholastica was a devoted follower of Christ and the twin sister of St. Benedict, the founder of Western monasticism. She established the Women's Benedictine order and dedicated her life to prayer, teaching, and the spiritual growth of her sisters. Her life exemplified the harmony of contemplation and service, influencing many within the faith.
prayer: I beg you, do not deprive me of your presence.

name: Sebastian
tagline: St. Sebastian was a Christian martyr who inspired many through his unwavering faith and courage.
description: St. Sebastian was born in Rome and became a soldier of the Roman Empire. His strong Christian faith compelled him to secretly help imprisoned Christians, which ultimately led to his martyrdom. He is often depicted tied to a tree and shot with arrows, symbolizing his steadfastness in the face of persecution.
prayer: Your faith is your shield, and your conviction is your sword.

name: Seraphim of Sarov
tagline: One of the most beloved Russian mystics, known for his joy and hospitality to all.
description: Seraphim lived as a hermit in the forest for 25 years. He spent a thousand nights standing on a rock in prayer. Later, he opened his door to pilgrims, greeting everyone with the words 'My joy, Christ is risen!' He emphasized the 'acquisition of the Holy Spirit' as the goal of the Christian life.
prayer: My joy, I pray you, acquire a peaceful spirit, and then thousands around you will be saved.

name: Seraphim of Vyritsa
tagline: A wealthy merchant who gave away his fortune after the Revolution to become a monk and a spiritual elder.
description: Vasily Muravyov was a successful businessman/milionaire who entered a monastery with his wife (who became a nun). During WWII, he prayed for 1,000 nights on a rock for the salvation of Russia, mirroring his namesake St. Seraphim of Sarov. He became a beloved elder to whom thousands of people from Leningrad flocked for comfort.
prayer: The most important thing is to love God and your neighbor.

name: Sergius of Radonezh
tagline: The greatest spiritual leader of medieval Russia and founder of the Trinity Lavra.
description: Sergius was a humble monk who revitalized Russian monasticism. He was known for his extreme poverty, his love for work, and his ability to reconcile quarreling princes, helping to unite Russia during the Mongol yoke.
prayer: Love God and love one another.

name: Severinus
tagline: Known for his ascetic life and miraculous deeds as a monk and missionary in the region that is now Austria.
description: St. Severinus was a wandering monk who dedicated his life to spreading Christianity among the pagan tribes of the Danube region. He became famous for his miraculous interventions, including restoring health to the sick and boosting the harvest during famine. His legacy as a holy man has rendered him a highly revered figure in Austrian Catholic tradition.
prayer: To serve God is the greatest joy of life.

name: Sharbel Makhlouf
tagline: Feast of the finding of St. Charbel's incorrupt body, celebrated in some Maronite traditions.
description: This feast commemorates the discovery of St. Charbel's incorrupt body when his tomb was opened and a mysterious light was seen above it. His body had been buried for months but showed no signs of decomposition, leading to increased veneration and eventually his beatification and canonization.
prayer: The silence of God is the loudest sound.

name: Simeon
tagline: He is known for being the first Christian martyr in Jerusalem.
description: St. Simeon was an early Christian leader who played a pivotal role in the spread of the faith during the first century. He is often remembered for his unwavering commitment to Christ, culminating in his martyrdom for his beliefs. His legacy continues to inspire Christians to stand firm in their faith despite challenges.
prayer: Faith is the light that shines in the dark.

name: Simon the Apostle
tagline: A dedicated apostle known for his fervent zeal for Christ and missionary work.
