description: St. Simon the Zealot was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus, distinguished by his passionate commitment to spreading the gospel. After the Ascension of Christ, he traveled extensively, with missionary efforts reportedly leading him to Persia. His legacy endures as a testament to faith and courage in the face of adversity.
prayer: If I could be the martyr whose blood would make the whole world believe in Jesus, I would welcome it.

name: Sixtus II
tagline: Pope and martyr known for his leadership during the early Church's struggles.
description: St. Sixtus II served as pope during a tumultuous time when Christians faced severe persecution under the Roman Empire. He was known for his courageous defense of the faith and his role in promoting the martyrdom of clergy and laity alike. Ultimately, he was martyred while celebrating the Eucharist, exemplifying his commitment to Christ and the Church.
prayer: The blood of martyrs is the seed of the Church.

name: Solanus Casey
tagline: He was an American Capuchin friar recognized for his gift of healing and service to the community.
description: Blessed Solanus Casey dedicated his life to serving others with humility and compassion. Known for his incredible faith and healing abilities, he became a beloved figure among those who sought his counsel and intercessions. His legacy of patience in the face of trials continues to inspire many today.
prayer: We should always pray for what we need, but we must never forget to thank God for what we have.

name: Stanislaus
tagline: A bishop and martyr who stood against the excesses of the monarchy in Poland.
description: St. Stanislaus was a prominent bishop of Krakow who fiercely defended the rights of the Church against the corrupt practices of the Polish king Bolesław II. His unwavering conviction and moral courage ultimately led to his martyrdom around the year 1079. Today, he is remembered not only as a protector of the faith but also as a symbol of justice and integrity in Poland.
prayer: As a shepherd, I must ensure my flock is safe from the wolves.

name: Stanislaus Kostka
tagline: A devoted Polish Jesuit novice who journeyed 450 miles to join the Jesuits.
description: St. Stanislaus Kostka was a young Polish Jesuit novice known for his unwavering faith and determination. After experiencing a profound spiritual calling, he traveled 450 miles to join the Jesuit order, despite facing numerous obstacles. His short life was marked by extraordinary devotion to God and the Virgin Mary, inspiring many to pursue holiness.
prayer: I long to see Jesus, my love and my goal.

name: Stanley Rother
tagline: An American priest martyred in Guatemala while serving the indigenous people.
description: Born in Oklahoma, Stanley Rother became a beloved priest in Guatemala, dedicating his life to serving the local indigenous population. His unwavering commitment to his community during a period of violent persecution led to his martyrdom in 1981. Rother's legacy of love and service continues to inspire many to this day.
prayer: I have no greater gift than to give my life for others.

name: Stephen
tagline: St. Stephen is recognized as the first Christian martyr, who was stoned to death for his faith.
description: St. Stephen was one of the first seven deacons appointed in the early Church, chosen for his faith and wisdom. His unwavering devotion to Christ and his eloquent defense of the faith led to his martyrdom outside Jerusalem, making him a powerful symbol of conviction. His legacy inspires countless Christians today to stand firm in their beliefs, even in the face of persecution.
prayer: Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.

name: Sylvester
tagline: Known for being the Pope who led the Church during the first half of the 4th century.
description: St. Sylvester was the pope who presided over the Church during a time of significant growth and transition. He is celebrated for his role in the Council of Nicaea, which addressed the Arian controversy. Pope Sylvester's leadership laid the foundation for the future of the Church in a rapidly changing world.
prayer: Faith is the entrance to the life of Christ.

name: Symphorian
tagline: St. Symphorian is known for his unwavering faith in the face of persecution and his inspirational martyrdom.
description: St. Symphorian was a young Christian martyr from the second century, who remained steadfast in his faith despite persecution. He was arrested and ultimately executed for refusing to renounce his beliefs. His bravery and commitment to Christ inspire many to embrace their faith with courage and conviction.
prayer: The glory of God is man fully alive.

name: Tekle Haymanot
tagline: The most celebrated Ethiopian saint, a monk and missionary who spread Christianity throughout southern Ethiopia.
description: St. Tekle Haymanot was an Ethiopian monk who founded the monastery of Debre Libanos, which became the most important monastic center in Ethiopian Christianity. He is credited with converting many pagan communities and is venerated as a national saint.
prayer: Prayer is the breath of the soul.

name: Teresa Benedicta
tagline: A Jewish convert to Catholicism who became a Carmelite philosopher and was martyred at Auschwitz.
description: Born Edith Stein in Germany, she was a brilliant philosopher who converted to Catholicism and took the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross. As a Carmelite nun, she dedicated her life to prayer and contemplation before ultimately being arrested and sent to Auschwitz during World War II for her Jewish heritage. Her profound writings on faith and philosophy have inspired countless individuals in their spiritual journeys.
prayer: The nation doesn’t simply live in its people

name: Teresa of Avila
tagline: Mystic of the Interior Castle
description: St. Teresa of Avila was a Carmelite reformer and Doctor of the Church who mapped the soul's journey to God through her Interior Castle. Practical yet profoundly mystical, she combined administrative genius with ecstatic prayer.
prayer: Let nothing disturb you. Let nothing frighten you. All things are passing away. God never changes. Patience obtains all things.

name: Teresa of the Andes
tagline: A Chilean Discalced Carmelite nun who died at 19, known for her profound joy and mystical union with God.
description: St. Teresa of the Andes, born Juanita Fernández Solar, was a Chilean girl from a wealthy family who entered the Discalced Carmelite convent in Los Andes at age 18. She lived only 11 months as a Carmelite before dying of typhus, but her diary and letters reveal an extraordinary mystical life. She was the first Chilean saint.
prayer: God is infinite joy.

name: Thecla
tagline: St. Thecla is known for her remarkable dedication to the Christian faith and her role as one of the earliest female martyrs.
description: St. Thecla was a young woman from Iconium who, inspired by the teachings of St. Paul, embraced a life of celibacy and devotion to God. She faced persecution for her faith, enduring trials that ultimately led to her martyrdom. Her story has inspired generations, symbolizing the strength and resilience of women in the early church.
prayer: For I will not marry, but I will follow my hope, which has been spoken of unto me.

name: Theodore of Sykeon
tagline: He is known for his ascetic life and numerous miraculous healings.
description: St. Theodore of Sykeon was a Byzantine monk renowned for his piety and deep commitment to an ascetic lifestyle. He spent his life in seclusion, dedicating himself to prayer and spiritual healing, earning a reputation for performing miracles. His legacy continues to inspire those seeking holiness and devotion in the Christian faith.
prayer: Prayer is the mother of all virtues.

name: Therese of Lisieux
tagline: The Little Flower
description: St. Therese of Lisieux discovered her "Little Way" — doing small things with great love. A Carmelite nun who died at 24, her spiritual autobiography became one of the most influential books in Catholic history. She is patron saint of missionaries despite never leaving her convent.
prayer: Miss no single opportunity of making some small sacrifice, here by a smiling look, there by a kindly word; always doing the smallest right and doing it all for love.

name: Thomas Aquinas
tagline: The Angelic Doctor
description: St. Thomas Aquinas harmonized faith and reason in his monumental Summa Theologica. A Dominican friar of towering intellect, he showed that truth is one — whether discovered through philosophy or revelation. Near the end of his life, a mystical experience led him to call his writings "mere straw."
prayer: Grant me, O Lord my God, a mind to know you, a heart to seek you, wisdom to find you, conduct pleasing to you, faithful perseverance in waiting for you, and a hope of finally embracing you.

name: Thomas Becket
tagline: Martyrdom for the independence of the Church.
description: St. Thomas Becket was the Archbishop of Canterbury who fiercely contested the authority of King Henry II over the church. His dedication to church independence led to a dramatic confrontation resulting in his martyrdom. Today, he is remembered as a symbol of religious freedom and integrity in leadership.
prayer: I am ready to die for my country, but I will not betray my church.

name: Thomas More
tagline: St. Thomas More was a Lord Chancellor of England who was martyred for his unwavering faith and refusal to accept King Henry VIII's authority over the Church.
description: St. Thomas More was a renowned English lawyer, philosopher, and author known for his strong moral conviction. As Lord Chancellor, he stood firm against the Act of Supremacy, ultimately leading to his execution in 1535. His life exemplifies integrity and steadfastness in faith amidst political turmoil.
prayer: I die the king's good servant, but God's first.

name: Thomas the Apostle
tagline: The apostle famously known for his skepticism regarding Christ’s resurrection.
description: St. Thomas the Apostle, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, is best known for his initial doubt about the resurrection. He traveled to India, where he played a pivotal role in establishing Christian communities. His unwavering faith following his encounter with the risen Christ led to his martyrdom, and he is honored as the patron saint of India.
prayer: My Lord and my God!

name: Timothy
tagline: Timothy was a devoted bishop and close disciple of St. Paul, known for his contributions to the early Church.
description: St. Timothy, a key figure in the early Christian church, served as the bishop of Ephesus. He was a trusted companion of St. Paul, receiving two epistles that provide guidance and insight into his pastoral role. His commitment to leading his community with grace marked him as a model for Christian leadership.
prayer: Let no one despise your youth, but set the believers an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.

name: Titus
tagline: St. Titus was a close companion of St. Paul and played a significant role in the early Christian church as the Bishop of Crete.
description: St. Titus was one of the prominent figures of the early Church, entrusted by St. Paul to lead the Christian community in Crete. Known for his unwavering faith and strong leadership, he helped establish Christian practices in an area known for its challenges. His letters from St. Paul provide insights into the responsibilities and virtues expected of church leaders.
prayer: You must teach what is in accord with sound doctrine.

name: Toribio Romo González
tagline: A Mexican priest martyred during the Cristero War who has become the unofficial patron of migrants crossing the US-Mexico border.
description: St. Toribio Romo González was a young Mexican priest who was martyred during the Cristero War at age 28. In recent decades, countless Mexican and Central American migrants have reported seeing a mysterious young man who helped them cross the desert safely — they later identified him from pictures as St. Toribio.
prayer: Do not be afraid

name: Trophimus
tagline: He is primarily known for his role as a martyr and a companion to St. Paul in the early Church.
description: St. Trophimus is known as a companion of St. Paul, having served as a supporter in his ministry during the early Christian church. A devoted and tireless worker in spreading the Gospel, he was eventually martyred for his faith, exemplifying courage and conviction. His unwavering dedication to Christ and his compassion for the marginalized have made him a revered figure in the Catholic Church.
prayer: Faith is the anchor of the soul, firm and secure.

name: Turibius of Mogrovejo
tagline: Archbishop of Lima who evangelized Peru and defended indigenous rights.
description: St. Turibius of Mogrovejo was a Spanish priest who became the Archbishop of Lima during the Spanish colonization of South America. He tirelessly worked to evangelize the indigenous peoples and fought for their rights against colonial injustices. His dedication to reforming the Church and promoting justice has made him a revered figure in the history of Peru.
prayer: A true pastor must not only think of his own salvation, but also of that of his flock.

name: Ursula
tagline: A legendary British princess who traveled across Europe with 11,000 virgins and was martyred by the Huns.
description: Ursula's story is one of the most famous legends of the Middle Ages. She led a group of young women on a pilgrimage to Rome. On their return trip, they were intercepted at Cologne by the Huns, who martyred them when they refused to renounce their faith or marry the Hun army.
prayer: We follow the King of Kings.

name: Valentine
tagline: A priest who defied Emperor Claudius II by marrying couples in secret, resulting in his martyrdom.
description: St. Valentine was a Roman priest renowned for his courage in marrying couples during a time when such unions were prohibited by the emperor. His dedication to love and faith ultimately led to his imprisonment and execution. Today, he is celebrated as the patron saint of lovers, symbolizing commitment and hope.
prayer: Love is the martyrdom of a Christ.

name: Veronica
tagline: St. Veronica is best known for compassionately wiping the face of Jesus on his way to Calvary, resulting in the image of His face miraculously being imprinted on her cloth.
description: St. Veronica is remembered for her act of kindness towards Jesus during His Passion. Her bravery and devotion led her to defy the crowd to offer Him comfort in His time of suffering. This encounter not only solidified her place in Christian tradition but also established her as a symbol of compassion and empathy.
prayer: In my heart, Lord, I carry Your passion.

name: Vincent
tagline: He is known for his courageous stand for the faith during the persecution of Christians.
description: St. Vincent was one of the early Christian martyrs, known for his unwavering faith in the face of severe torture and persecution. He served as a deacon in the early Church and became a symbol of strength and endurance for Christians throughout the centuries. His martyrdom inspired many to remain steadfast in their beliefs, and he continues to be celebrated as a heroic figure in Christianity.
prayer: Always be prepared to speak for God's truth.

name: Vincent de Paul
tagline: He dedicated his life to serving the poor and founded the Vincentians and the Daughters of Charity.
description: St. Vincent de Paul was a French priest renowned for his commitment to helping the impoverished and vulnerable. He established the Congregation of the Mission and the Daughters of Charity, organizations that continue to serve communities worldwide. His legacy of compassion and service inspired many to dedicate their lives to acts of charity.
prayer: It's not enough to give from our abundance

name: Vincent Ferrer
tagline: St. Vincent Ferrer was a remarkable Dominican preacher known for his fervent evangelization efforts and miraculous deeds.
description: Born in Valencia, Spain, St. Vincent Ferrer became a powerful preacher who traveled across Europe, spreading the Christian faith during a tumultuous period. He is renowned for his miraculous healings and prophetic visions, inspiring countless followers. His legacy endures as a vital figure in the Dominican Order and the history of the Church.
prayer: The devil can do nothing against a man who is living in grace.

name: Virgil of Salzburg
tagline: Being the Bishop of Salzburg who contributed to the spread of Christianity in the region and was known for his scholarly work.
description: St. Virgil was a learned monk who served as Bishop of Salzburg during the 8th century. He played a crucial role in the establishment of the church in Bavaria and was instrumental in the evangelization of the surrounding areas. A man of deep faith and intellect, he is remembered for his dedication to both education and pastoral care.
prayer: Faith is the compass that guides us through the storms of life.

name: Vladimir of Kiev
tagline: The Grand Prince of Kiev who converted to Christianity and baptized the entire nation of Kievan Rus'.
description: Vladimir was a fierce pagan ruler who sent envoys to research different religions. They were so moved by the beauty of the liturgy in Constantinople that he chose Orthodoxy. After his conversion, he radically changed his life, dismissing his many wives and building churches and hospitals.
prayer: I have found the true faith.

name: Walburga
tagline: An Anglo-Saxon missionary nun who helped evangelize Germany and became one of the most venerated saints of the medieval period.
description: St. Walburga was an Anglo-Saxon princess who left England to join her brothers Sts. Willibald and Winebald in their missionary work in Germany. She became abbess of the double monastery of Heidenheim and was renowned for her healing powers and educational work. She is one of the most celebrated women missionaries of the 8th century.
prayer: Where there is faith, there is light.

name: Wasnildus
tagline: St. Wasnildus is recognized for his pious life and dedication to monasticism.
description: St. Wasnildus was a revered monk who devoted his life to prayer and contemplation in a secluded monastery. His deep spirituality and commitment to asceticism inspired many of his contemporaries. Known for his wisdom, he guided numerous souls on their spiritual journeys throughout his life.
prayer: Contemplation is a treasure that lies within the heart.

name: Wenceslaus
tagline: St. Wenceslaus was a Duke of Bohemia who was martyred by his brother in defense of his Christian faith.
description: St. Wenceslaus, revered as the patron saint of the Czech Republic, is known for his leadership during a challenging time for Christianity in Central Europe. Despite familial betrayal, he remained steadfast in promoting the Christian faith and justice. His legacy endures in the hearts of the Czech people, symbolizing courage and devotion.
prayer: I will not let the wrongs of others take away my righteousness.

name: William
tagline: He is known for his extensive work in reforming monastic life and promoting the Benedictine Rule.
description: St. William was a committed Benedictine monk and later became the Bishop of Eboracum, known today as York. He devoted his life to the care of his flock, emphasizing the need for pastoral charity and the importance of monastic reform. His canonization highlighted his role as a shining example of holiness and compassion in the Middle Ages.
prayer: For where there is charity and wisdom, there is neither fear nor ignorance.

name: William of Bourges
tagline: He is known for his contributions to the church as the Archbishop of Bourges and for his commitment to church reform.
description: St. William of Bourges served as Archbishop in the early 13th century, where he worked tirelessly to reform the clerical state and improve church practices. He was deeply dedicated to the poor, providing them with aid and support during his tenure. His legacy is remembered for the influence he had on both the church and society in France.
prayer: The greatest gift one can give is the gift of love.

name: William of Eskhill
tagline: William was a devoted hermit known for his ascetic life and deep spirituality.
description: St. William of Eskhill was a revered hermit who dedicated his life to prayer and contemplation in the wilderness. Through his rigorous ascetic practices, he sought to grow closer to God and inspire others toward holiness. His legacy of devotion continues to inspire many on the path of spiritual growth.
prayer: Prayer is the root of all virtues.

name: William of York
tagline: He is known for his dedication to the Church and his conflict with the powers of his time regarding his rightful position.
description: St. William of York was a Benedictine monk and later became the Archbishop of York. His life was marked by a struggle to reclaim his see against political intrigue and opposition. After his death, he was regarded as a martyr for his unwavering commitment to his faith and his flock.
prayer: In all things, I have followed the truth with a sincere heart.

name: Willibald
tagline: He is known for his missionary work and founding of several churches in Germany.
description: St. Willibald was an English monk who set out on a pilgrimage to the Holy Land. His travels took him across Europe, where he shared the Christian faith and established monasteries. His dedication to spreading the Gospel and his commitment to the monastic life made him a revered figure in early Christianity.
prayer: May your heart be a vessel of love and your hands a source of kindness.

name: Willibrord
tagline: Known as the apostle of the Frisians, he was instrumental in spreading Christianity in the region of what is now the Netherlands.
description: St. Willibrord was a Benedictine monk from England who became a missionary in the continental Europe during the early Middle Ages. He founded several churches and established the diocese of Utrecht, becoming its first bishop. His dedicated work in evangelizing the Frisians earned him the title of a revered saint in both local and broader Christian contexts.
prayer: The glory of God is the human person fully alive.

name: Wolfgang
tagline: He is known for his role in the Christianization of the region of Bavaria and for founding several monasteries.
description: St. Wolfgang was a Benedictine monk and the Bishop of Regensburg known for his missionary work in Bavaria. He dedicated his life to spreading Christianity and educating the people in his diocese. His legacy includes various churches and abbeys established in his honor throughout the region.
prayer: The Lord has given me a true friendship.

name: Yves
tagline: St. Yves is known for his unwavering commitment to justice and the defense of the poor.
description: St. Yves, a Breton priest and lawyer, dedicated his life to serving the underprivileged and offering fair legal representation. His work emphasized the importance of compassion and integrity in legal matters. He is revered as a champion of justice and is often invoked for guidance in legal issues.
prayer: The law should be based on the truth.

name: Zélie Martin
tagline: Mother of St. Thérèse of Lisieux and a successful businesswoman who raised a family of extraordinary holiness.
description: St. Zélie Martin (née Guérin) was a French lace-maker and mother of nine children, five of whom became nuns, including St. Thérèse of Lisieux. She ran a successful Alençon lace business while raising her family with deep Catholic devotion. She died of breast cancer at age 45 and was canonized alongside her husband in 2015.
prayer: I want to become a saint, and for that I must suffer much.

name: Zita
tagline: She is known for her unwavering devotion and service to her family and the poor.
description: St. Zita was born in Tuscany, Italy, and dedicated her life to serving her family and those in need. She worked as a servant for the wealthy Fatinelli family, embodying kindness and humility in her daily tasks. Celebrated for her virtuous life, she became a beloved saint, and her example inspires many who work in domestic service.
prayer: A mother’s love would give her life to save her child.
